Chars voices funny cartoon characters (a cheeky time-traveller, khans, princes, tsars, servants, nobles, officers, an empress): short, punchy, expressive, following the bracketed style tags.
lines: Then the Mongols turned around and went home. No great battle. The yoke just... ended.
Ivan the Third tripled Moscow's land. He married Sophia, niece of the last emperor of Constantinople, and took the empire's symbol: the double-headed eagle.
Moscow now called itself the Third Rome. Chaos had produced... total control. Again.
And her traders crossed the Pacific. In seventeen eighty-four, Russians built their first permanent settlement in a faraway place called... Alaska.
[checking his watch, grinning] Ooh. Remember that one. We know how this ends.
But for most Russians, life got harder. Millions of peasants were serfs, owned by landlords, bought and sold with the land.
In seventeen seventy-three, a Cossack called Pugachev claimed to be the dead Peter the Third, and led a huge peasant uprising across the Volga. It took two years to crush.
Freedom for the nobles, control for everyone else. The loop, in a powdered wig.
[to camera] By the way, if you're enjoying this, subscribe. It's free, and it makes the time machine run.
When Catherine died in seventeen ninety-six, Russia was a giant on Europe's stage.
And in the west, a short French general was about to test exactly how big that giant really was.

lines: The new government then made one fatal mistake. It kept fighting the war.
And a bald, furious revolutionary named Vladimir Lenin promised Russians exactly what they wanted: Peace. Land. Bread.
Comrade Lenin, our slogan. "Peace, land, bread"?
And when do we deliver the peace?
In October nineteen seventeen, Lenin's Bolsheviks seized power.
Then came a brutal civil war: Lenin's Reds against the anti-communist Whites. Britain, France, America and Japan all sent troops. Millions died from fighting, hunger and disease.
In July nineteen eighteen, in a cellar in the city of Yekaterinburg, the Bolsheviks shot Nicholas, Alexandra, their four daughters, their son Alexei, and their servants.
The Reds won. And in nineteen twenty-two, the old empire became a brand new country: the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. The USSR.
[checking his watch] Collapse... then a new man promises order. You know what comes next.

lines: Alexander reformed the courts, the army, local government. And on March the thirteenth, eighteen eighty-one, he approved a plan that could have been Russia's first step towards an elected assembly.
That same afternoon, revolutionaries threw a bomb at his carriage. It missed. Alexander stepped out to check on the wounded... and a second bomber threw another, right at his feet.
[quietly] The tsar who freed the serfs. Killed the day he tried to give people a voice.
His son tore up the plan. The loop was back on its old setting. And the tsar after that... would be the last one.
So look back at the whole story.
The Slavs invited the Vikings, because of chaos.
Moscow learned total control from the Mongols.
The Time of Troubles gave Russia the Romanovs.
The fall of the tsars gave Russia Lenin and Stalin.
And the chaos of the nineties gave Russia Putin.
Eleven hundred years. Different hats. Same story.
[looking at his watch, then at the camera] Will Russia ever break the loop?
Nobody knows. Maybe not even the Russians.

[grinning, winding his watch] And if you thought Russia's rulers were rough on their own families... wait until you meet the Ottomans. Their sultans had a law that let them kill their own brothers. See you there.
